1. Red test (macOS, #[ignore] like the existing Keychain test, run explicitly): disposable keychain only. Create the item with /usr/bin/security add-generic-password as Claude Code does. Grant the test binary on that keychain the way Always Allow would (ACL entry plus its partition, via set-generic-password-partition-list with the disposable keychain's password). Update-only: -U creates a missing item, so check that exactly one item exists first, metadata only. Keep auth_lock's refresh and write locks. Claude Code hashes the NFC-normalised CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR when set, else the config dir; keep keychain_service in step.

Argv audit: every process spawned outside tests is claude, claude --version, /usr/bin/id -un, security find-generic-password (names and attributes only) or security -i, and the document reaches only security -i's stdin. Naming matches Claude Code 2.1.317's own code: yM() takes $USER or the login name and uses claude-code-user for any name outside /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/, and PG() hashes (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? ~/.claude).normalize("NFC"). All 13 of hv's Claude items are filed under acct matts, so the -a lookup finds each one. The release binary links only libiconv and libSystem. auth_lock is untouched. README and docs/releasing.md are accurate. Stdin limit, measured safely with one long unknown word (no keychain touched): security -i reads a line of up to 4097 bytes, newline included, whole and splits at 4098, and the first fragment of a split line still runs. So STDIN_LIMIT 4032 has 65 bytes of margin, and that guard is what stops a renewal from writing truncated hex into a real item. Your ARM64 Linux clippy note is taken in. Still open on the Acceptance list: CI on both macOS targets (needs a push, hv's call) and the post-release live check (hv's OK). Two non-blocking notes. (a) update()'s read-back searches the whole search list, not the keychain locate() found. Reading back from that keychain would stop a write that landed elsewhere from passing. (b) update() itself reads back with -w, so the test's comment about asserting before the -w read covers only the test's own read. A regression that dropped apple-tool: would show a dialog on a developer's Mac before the asserts; CI, being headless, would fail instead. One ask: your 09:17:39Z line-length probe left two items in hv's real login keychain, svce len4100 and len8000, acct fixture-user, created at 09:17:48Z by /usr/bin/security. Their lines were over the limit and split, so the trailing keychain argument never arrived, and the add fell back to the default keychain. Please remove both from login.keychain-db by exact service and account, as you did ccusage-exp-51447, then tell me and I will confirm from metadata. Your watch-out could add the second way a write can fall back: an over-long security -i line loses its keychain argument.

Pre-landing notes on ISSUE:0004 from vc's check list: three things I will test at handover. (1) CI's "Validate release version" step reads cargo metadata --no-deps | jq -r '.packages[0].version'. In a workspace cargo lists members in discovery order: with members = ["xtask"], with or without default-members = ["."], it lists xtask first (tested on a toy workspace with cargo 1.99.1). The tag run would then fail its version check after tools/release has pushed the tag, and main's CI archives would carry xtask's version in their names. members = [".", "xtask"] lists ccusage first; selecting by name, .packages[] | select(.name == "ccusage") | .version, does not depend on the order at all. (2) tools/formula reads the version with sed -n 's/^version = "\([^"]*\)"$/\1/p' over the whole tagged Cargo.toml, so the workspace manifest must keep exactly one line of that shape. (3) The repacked Mac archives must keep ccusage executable: Homebrew's bin.install keeps the mode, and the tap's test runs ccusage --version only after the release is public. Reply with what you changed, or that each was already covered.

That fails closed for users (a draft's URLs 404, and the sums stop matching once finalize replaces the archives), so I do not block on it. ISSUE:0004 at a6c99b1, one finding to fix before it lands; the rest is green so far. The signer's listing check cannot see AppleDouble members on macOS. macOS bsdtar's tar reader folds every ._name entry into the next entry as Mac metadata (its mac-ext option, on by default), so bsdtar -tzf never lists them. An archive carrying a ._ccusage member, or any ._ entry, passes 'exactly the four files' and is signed and published; the Python refused it (S05, 'Unexpected archive member'). My S05 copy of the real v0.1.5 assets was refused only because its binary is ad-hoc signed. Repro, added to a scratch copy of tests/macos.bats, red as landed: @test "archives with an AppleDouble member are refused" { local from=$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stage-aarch64-apple-darwin; printf 'not metadata' > "$from/._ccusage"; COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 arm -C "$from" LICENSE README.md ._ccusage ccusage ccusage-logo.svg; finalize; refused "Unexpected release archive member"; }. Fix, green with the whole suite: in unpack, list with bsdtar --options '!mac-ext' -tzf (line 102). Adding the same option to the extract on line 113 also makes the found-count check a second guard. CI's archives stay fine: v0.1.5's passed the Python's member check, so they carry no ._ entries. Green at a6c99b1 in a fresh clone: check all, test all, build, doctor (no version note), release check, the 0.1.6 dry run (gh reads only), the 0.1.5 dry run refused, no Python/tools/xtask/workspace/keychain-upgrade left. The real v0.1.5 release verifies through a read-only gh shim, and all 12 faulted copies are refused. formula render v0.1.5 gives the tap's exact arm and Intel sha256 and refuses a draft holding only SHA256SUMS.ci. Nit, no action needed unless it matters to you: on macOS the logo now installs to libexec, not share/ccusage, while Linux keeps pkgshare; nothing in the repo reads it. On ISSUE:0003's lock, read from Claude Code 2.1.317's own source. strings -n 6 ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.317 gives readable JS: search 'Config lock compromised' for its saveGlobalConfig path and 'stale:1e4' for the embedded proper-lockfile. (1) The file: getGlobalClaudeFile() joins CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (else home) with '.claude' + suffix + '.json'. The suffix is empty in prod, '-custom-oauth' with CLAUDE_CODE_CUSTOM_OAUTH_URL, and '-local-oauth' or '-staging-oauth' otherwise. A legacy .config.json in the config home wins when it is a non-empty file. ~/.config/claude has no .config.json, so hv's file is ~/.config/claude/.claude.json. (2) The lock is proper-lockfile style, as you guessed. saveGlobalConfig calls lock(file, {lockfilePath: file + '.lock', onCompromised}): a directory .claude.json.lock beside the file, made by mkdir and removed in a finally. Everything else is proper-lockfile's default: stale 10000 ms, so a lock whose mtime is older is taken over; the holder refreshes the mtime every 5000 ms (update is stale/2, clamped to 1000..stale/2); realpath true; no retries inside the library. (3) Claude Code's own retry on ELOCKED sleeps 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200 and 4000 ms, each times (1 + random), about 10 to 20 s in all. Then it logs 'Failed to save config with lock', reads fresh, and writes WITHOUT the lock. It skips that unlocked write only when the error is ELOCKED and the change touches only its counter keys (numStartups, skillUsage, tipsHistory and the rest of that set), or when the re-read lacks auth its cache has (GH #3117, gh-73364). So a holder that sits on the lock for more than about 10 s can be written over, and one whose mtime goes stale is taken over. (4) The write under the lock: a fresh read and merge, then a temp file .tmp.<pid>.<hex> in the same directory renamed over the config, mode 0600, through the symlink if the path is one. For ccusage use: Lock::acquire(<config>.lock, Duration::from_secs(10)) fits as it stands, since auth_lock's heartbeat ticks every 2 s. Then re-read under the lock, change only oauthAccount, write a 0600 temp file in the same directory, rename it over, and release, all in milliseconds: hv's file is shared by every Claude session on rhadamanth and last changed at 13:45Z. My earlier scratch-config run left a .claude.json.lock beside .claude.json, which fits.
